The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Türkiye, Mevlüt Çavuşoğlu has arrived in the Maldives today, on an Official visit, on the invitation of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid.

Minister Çavuşoğlu was received at the Velana International Airport by Minister Shahid and senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

During this visit, Minister Çavuşoğlu will be paying courtesy calls on the President of the Republic of Maldives, Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and Speaker of the People’s Majlis, President Mohamed Nasheed. Minister Çavuşoğlu will also hold official talks with the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid.

This is the first Official visit from a Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Türkiye and marks an important milestone in the four decade long bilateral relationship between the Maldives and Türkiye.

en.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Türkiye to make an official visit to Maldives
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Türkiye to make an official visit to Maldives
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Türkiye to make an official visit to Maldives

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Türkiye, Mevlüt Çavuşoğlu will make an official visit to the Maldives from 28 – 30 January 2022, on the invitation of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid.

During this visit, Minister Çavuşoğlu will pay a courtesy call on the President of the Republic of Maldives, Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and Speaker of the People’s Majlis, President Mohamed Nasheed. Minister Çavuşoğlu will also hold official talks with his counterpart Minister Shahid and sign a number of key agreements between Maldives and Türkiye.

This visit will mark the first ever official visit to the Maldives by a Turkish Foreign Minister.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Australia Day greetings
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Australia Day greetings
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Australia Day greetings

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends message of felicitations to Marise Payne, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Commonwealth of Australia on the occasion of Australia Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government, the people of the Republic of Maldives and on my own behalf, I would like to extend warm greetings and sincere best wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of the Commonwealth of Australia, on the occasion of Australia Day.

Over the years, Australia has remained a close partner contributing immensely to the socio-economic advancement of the Maldives. The Maldives highly values its close relationship with Australia. The bond we share is grounded in mutual respect, sincerity, and trust. I firmly believe that the close cordial ties between our two countries will continue to prosper in the years to come.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your good health and well-being, and for further progress of the people of the Commonwealth of Australia and the assurances of my highest considerations.”

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Republic Day greetings to India
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Republic Day greetings to India
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Republic Day greetings to India

Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sent a message of felicitations to Dr. S. Jaishankar, Minister of External Affairs of India, on the occassion of the 73rd Republic Day of India.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government and people of Maldives, I have great pleasure in conveying to Your Excellency and the friendly people of the Republic of India our sincere felicitations and good wishes on the occasion of the 73rd Republic Day of India.

For 73 years, the Constitution of India has provided a framework of governance and guaranteed rights to over a billion people comprising the world’s largest democracy. This monumental achievement provides inspiration and hope, to countries all over the world undertaking their own democratic journeys.

The many gestures of goodwill, humanitarian assistance and friendship provided by the Government of India is a true testament to the longstanding ties between the Maldives and India. India continues to prove that it is, and always will be, the first responder in any crisis in the Maldives. We remain committed to uphold an ‘India First Policy’, and appreciate India’s ‘Neighbourhood First Policy’, which has worked to the mutual benefit of both our countries. We will also continue to cooperate on issues of mutual interest in the international arena.

May I also take this opportunity to convey my personal good wishes for your health and well-being, and for the continued progress and prosperity of the friendly people of India. Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid holds a telephone conversation with the Foreign Minister of Saudi Arabia
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid holds a telephone conversation with the Foreign Minister of Saudi Arabia
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid holds a telephone conversation with the Foreign Minister of Saudi Arabia

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid had a telephone conversation with his Saudi counterpart, His Royal Highness Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, this evening.

During the telephone conversation, the two Ministers discussed ways to further enhance the strong spirit of cooperation between the two friendly nations and discussed the ongoing developmental projects in the Maldives, being carried out with the assistance from the Government of Saudi Arabia, through the Saudi Fund for Development.

During the call, Minister Shahid also confirmed the support of the Government of Maldives for Saudi Arabia’s proposal to host the World Expo 2030 in the city of Riyadh.

The two Foreign Ministers expressed their renewed commitment to strengthening the long-standing fraternal relationship between the Maldives and Saudi Arabia, and reaffirmed their confidence in working together on issues of mutual interest, both bilaterally and in the international fora.

en.title: New Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives calls on Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
en.description: New Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives calls on Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
en.body:
New Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives calls on Minister of State for Foreign Affairs

Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives, Her Excellency Takeuchi Midori called on the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today. Ambassador Takechi presented her credentials to President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih at a ceremony held at the President’s Office on 20 January 2022.

During the meeting, State Minister Khaleel congratulated the Ambassador on the presentation of credentials to the President, and expressed confidence that the long-standing ties between the two countries will be further strengthened during her tenure.

State Minister Khaleel expressed his profound appreciation for the continued assistance and co-operation received from Japan towards the socio-economic development of Maldives, especially during the fight against the Covid-19 pandemic.

State Minister Khaleel expressed his intention to take the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations this year as an opportunity to further elevate the Maldives-Japan relations to greater heights. Ambassador expressed her heartfelt gratitude for the warm welcome she received and stated that she is determined to strengthen bilateral cooperation between the countries.

State Minister was accompanied by Javed Faizal, Additional Secretary, Fathimath Naeema, Executive Director and Mohamed Shujau, Desk Officer at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

en.title: FOSIM holds Training Program on Protocol Etiquettes
en.description: FOSIM holds Training Program on Protocol Etiquettes
en.body:
FOSIM holds Training Program on Protocol Etiquettes

Foreign Service Institute of Maldives (FOSIM) held a training session on Basic Protocol Etiquettes for the staff of Ministry of National Planning, Housing and Infrastructure this morning.

A total of 15 participants from the Ministry of National Planning, Housing and Infrastructure participated in the training session. The session held virtually aimed at enabling participants to acquire basic and foundational knowledge and skills on diplomatic protocols, protocol etiquettes for them to function effectively in their respective work environment.

The session was conducted by the Protocol department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

en.title: New Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives calls on Foreign Secretary
en.description: New Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives calls on Foreign Secretary
en.body:
New Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives calls on Foreign Secretary

Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives, Her Excellency Takeuchi Midori called on the Foreign Secretary, His Excellency Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed today, following the Presentation of Credentials to His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, President of the Republic of Maldives in the morning.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Secretary congratulated the Ambassador on the Presentation of Credentials to the President, and expressed confidence that the close ties and friendship between Maldives and Japan will continue to prosper during her tenure.

The Foreign Secretary conveyed his appreciation for the continuous support and assistance provided to the people of Maldives, by the Government of Japan during the past 5 decades. Foreign Secretary also extended his appreciation for the generosity shown towards the Maldives in its ongoing efforts to combat the spread of COVID-19, emphasizing in particular the generous donations of 112,000 doses of AstraZeneca vaccines by the Government of Japan, facilitated through the WHO COVAX facility, which the Maldives received in 2021.

Foreign Secretary Ghafoor and Ambassador Takeuchi concurred to collaboratively cooperate toward further development of the bilateral relations, seizing the opportunity of the 55th Anniversary of diplomatic relations this year, and discussed ways to commemorate the occassion jointly both in Male and in Tokyo.

Ambassador expressed her heartfelt gratitude for the warm welcome she received and stated that she is determined to further enhance the bilateral relationship between Maldives and Japan.

Ambassador Takeuchi is the second female resident Ambassador from Japan to the Maldives, who takes over from Her Excellency Keiko Yanai who served as the previous Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives from January 2019 to December 2021.

Foreign Secretary was accompanied by Javed Faizal, Additional Secretary, Fathimath Naeema, Executive Director and Mohamed Shujau, Desk Officer at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

en.title: Maldives establishes Diplomatic Relations with Burundi
en.description: Maldives establishes Diplomatic Relations with Burundi
en.body:
Maldives establishes Diplomatic Relations with Burundi

The Republic of Maldives and the Republic of Burundi have formally established diplomatic relations today.

The Joint Communiqué formalising diplomatic relations between the two countries was signed on behalf of the Government of Maldives by Her Excellency Thilmeeza Hussain, Permanent Representative of the Republic of Maldives to the United Nations and on behalf of the Government of Burundi by His Excellency Zéphyrin Maniratanga, Permanent Representative of the Republic of Burundi to the United Nations. The Joint Communiqué was signed at a ceremony held at the Permanent Mission of the Republic of Maldives to the United Nations in New York.

Cultivating meaningful partnerships with friendly countries, based on mutual respect, is a key priority of the foreign policy of President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih.

As comparatively small nations in the international arena, the establishment of diplomatic relations between the the Maldives and Burundi paves the way for the two countries to cooperate further to achieve common goals in areas of shared interest. Following the establishment of diplomatic relations with Burundi, the Maldives currently maintains diplomatic relations with 179 countries.

Burundi is a landlocked country situated in Africa, with a population of approximately 11.89 million.

en.title: First Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Russia presents Credentials to the Russian Federation
en.description: First Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Russia presents Credentials to the Russian Federation
en.body:
First Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Russia presents Credentials to the Russian Federation

Ambassador of Maldives to the Federal Republic of Germany, His Excellency Ahmed Latheef presented his Letters of Credence, as the Non-Resident Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Maldives to the Russian Federation at a ceremony held at the Russian Embassy in Berlin today. His Excellency Sergey Nechaev, Ambassador of Russia to Germany, received the Letters of Credence issued by H. E. Mr. Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, President of the Republic of Maldives addressed to H. E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of Russia, under a special arrangement made due to the difficult Covid-19 pandemic travel restrictions.

During the meeting that followed the Credential Ceremony, Ambassador Nechaev congratulated Ambassador Latheef on the presentation of credentials as the first non-resident Ambassador from Maldives to Russia and expressed confidence that the long-standing ties between the two countries will be further strengthened during his tenure. Ambassador Latheef expressed his commitment to work closely with the Russian Government to enhance the bilateral relationship between both countries.

Ambassador Latheef also stated that the Government of Maldives is grateful for the significant contributions Russia has made towards the socio-economic development in the Maldives, particularly in the field of tourism. Tourism is the largest economic industry of the Maldives and Russia has always been a key tourism market, currently holding the second position of the tourist arrivals in the country with a total number of 222, 424 Russian tourists in 2021.

en.title: High Commissioner of India to Maldives calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.description: High Commissioner of India to Maldives calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.body:
High Commissioner of India to Maldives calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs

High Commissioner of India to Maldives, Munu Mahawar paid a courtesy call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, today.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Shahid congratulated and welcomed the High Commissioner and exchanged views on further elevating the longstanding relations of both countries. Both Minister Shahid and High Commissioner Mahawar also reviewed the ongoing developmental projects funded by Indian assistance and other cooperation programmes coordinated between Maldives and India.

Minister Shahid and High Commissioner Mahawar expressed satisfaction on the key milestones achieved in India-Maldives relations during the last three years under His Excellency President Solih’s administration. Minister Shahid extended his profound gratitude to the Government of India for the generous assistance provided during the challenging times of Covid-19 and noted that India is a country Maldives can always rely on in any time of need.

High Commissioner Mahawar thanked for the warm welcome, assured his strong commitment to work closely with the government of Maldives in strengthening the close ties between the two countries.

dv.title: އިންޑިއާ އަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ފަރާތްތަކުން ގޭގައި 7 ދުވަހުގެ ކަރަންޓީން ފުރިހަމަކުރަންޖެހޭ ގޮތަށް ހަމަޖެއްސުމާ ގުޅޭ
dv.description: އިންޑިއާ އަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ފަރާތްތަކުން ގޭގައި 7 ދުވަހުގެ ކަރަންޓީން ފުރިހަމަކުރަންޖެހޭ ގޮތަށް ހަމަޖެއްސުމާ ގުޅޭ
dv.body:
އިންޑިއާ އަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ފަރާތްތަކުން ގޭގައި 7 ދުވަހުގެ ކަރަންޓީން ފުރިހަމަކުރަންޖެހޭ ގޮތަށް ހަމަޖެއްސުމާ ގުޅޭ

ކޮވިޑް-19 ގެ އޮމިކްރޮން ވޭރިއަންޓް މުޅި ދުނިޔޭގައި ހަލުވިކަމާއެކު ފެތުރެމުން އަންނާތީ، އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުން އަޅަމުންގެންދާ ފިޔަވަޅުތައް އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމުގެ ގޮތުން، 11 ޖެނުއަރީ 2022 ވަނަ ދުވަހުގެ އިންޑިއާ ގަޑިން 00:01 ން ފެށިގެން އެ ގައުމަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ފަރާތްތައް 7 (ހަތެއް) ދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަށް ގޭގައި ކަރަންޓީނުވާންޖެހޭ ގޮތަށް ހަމަޖައްސައިފިއެވެ.

މިގޮތަށް ހަމަޖެއްސުމުގެ އިތުރަށް އެ ޤައުމަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ފަރާތްތައް އެ ޤައުމަށް ދަތުރުކުރުމުގެ ކުރިން 72 (ހަތްދިހަ ދޭއް) ގަޑިއިރުގެ ތެރޭގައި ހައްދާފައިވާ ކޮވިޑް-19 RT-PCR ނެގެޓިވް ޓެސްޓް ނަތީޖާ ހުށައަޅައި، ވޭތުވެދިޔަ 14 (ސާދަ) ދުވަހުގެ ތެރޭގައި ކޮށްފައިވާ ދަތުރުތަކުގެ މަޢުލޫމާތު ހިމަނައި، ހުށަހަޅާ މަޢުލޫމާތުގެ ޞައްޙަކަމަށާއި، ކޮވިޑާ ގުޅިގެން އެ ޤައުމުގެ ސަރުކާރުގެ ކަމާ ގުޅުންހުރި އިދާރާތަކުން އަޅާ ފިޔަވަޅުތަކަށް ފުރިހަމައަށް ޢަމަލު ކުރަން އިޤުރާރުވެ، އެކަމަށް ތައްޔާރުކޮށްފައިވާ "އެއަރ ސުވިދާ" ޕޯޓަލަށް ސެލްފް ޑެކްލަރޭޝަން ފޯމެއް ހުށަހަޅަންޖެހޭ ގޮތަށްވެސް ވަނީ ހަމަޖައްސާފައެވެ. 7 (ހަތެއް) ދުވަހުގެ ކަރަންޓީނަށްފަހު 8 (އަށެއް) ވަނަ ދުވަހު ހައްދާ ކޮވިޑް-19 RT-PCR ޓެސްޓުގެ ނަތީޖާ ނެގަޓިވް ވުމުން ގެއިން ނުކުމެވުނަސް، އިތުރު 7 (ހަތެއް) ދުވަސް ވަންދެން އެމީހެއްގެ ޞިއްޙަތު އަމިއްލައަށް މޮނިޓަރ ކުރަމުން ދާންޖެހޭނެއެވެ. އަދި މި ޓެސްޓުގެ ނަތީޖާ "އެއަރ ސުވިދާ" ޕޯޓަލްއަށް އަޕްލޯޑު ކުރަންޖެހޭނެއެވެ. އަދި މީގެ އިތުރުން، ކޮންމެ ފްލައިޓަކުން ދަތުރުކުރާ ފަސިންޖަރުންގެ ތެރެއިން %2 (އިންސައްތަ) މީހުން ރެންޑަމްކޮށް އެއަރޕޯޓުގައި ޓެސްޓްކުރާ ގޮތަށްވެސް އެ ޤައުމުގެ ސަރުކާރުންވަނީ ނިންމާފައެވެ.

މި ފިޔަވަޅުތައް މިގޮތަށް ހުރި ނަމަވެސް، އެ ޤައުމަށް، އެކުގައި ދަތުރުކުރާ 5 (ފަހެއް) އަހަރުން ދަށުގެ ކުދިން އޮން އެރައިވަލް އަދި ގޭގެ ކަރަންޓީން މުއްދަތަށްފަހު 8 (އަށެއް) ވަނަ ދުވަހުގެ ޓެސްޓު ހައްދާކަށް ނުޖެހޭނެއެވެ. ނަމަވެސް އެ ޤައުމަށް އެތެރެވާއިރު، ނުވަތަ ގޭގައި ކަރަންޓީންގައި ހުންނަ މުއްދަތުގައި ބަލީގެ އެއްވެސް އަލާމާތެއް ފެނިއްޖެނަމަ، ޓެސްޓު ހައްދައި ކޮވިޑް-19 އަށް ފައްސިވާ ފަރާތްތައް، އެކުލަވާލާފައިވާ އުސޫލުތަކާ އެއްގޮތަށް އެކަހެރިވެ ފަރުވާ ހޯދަންޖެހޭނެއެވެ.

ވީމާ، މި ފިޔަޅުތަކާގުޅިގެން، އިންޑިއާގައި ދިރިއުޅޭ އަދި އިންޑިއާއަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ދަތުރުކުރަން ޤަޞްދުކުރާ ފަރާތްތައް މިކަމަށް ސަމާލުވުމަށް އެދެމެވެ. އަދި މި ފިޔަވަޅުތަކަށް ބަދަލުއައުން އެކަށީގެންވުމާއެކު، ދަތުރުކުރުމުގެ ކުރިން މައުލޫމާތު ސާފުކުރުމަށްވެސް އެދެމެވެ.

މީގެ އިތުރުން، މި ދަނޑިވަޅުގައި ކޮންމެހެން ކުރަންޖެހޭ ދަތުރުތައް ފިޔަވައި، އެހެން ދަތުރުތައް ނުކުރުމަށް އިލްތިމާސްކުރަމެވެ. އަދި އިންޑިއާގައި ދިރިއުޅޭ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނާއި އެކިބޭނުންތަކަށް އިންޑިއާއަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުން އެޤައުމުގެ ސަރުކާރުގެ ނިންމުންތަކާއި އެންގުންތަކަށް ސަމާލުވުމަށްވެސް އިލްތިމާސްކުރަމެވެ.

en.title: Maldives and China Holds Official Talks
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid and Foreign Minister of China H.E. Wang Yi holds extensive bilateral discussions
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid and Foreign Minister of China H.E. Wang Yi holds extensive bilateral discussions

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, and the State Councilor and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People’s Republic of China, His Excellency Wang Yi, has held extensive bilateral discussions today at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

During the Official Talks, both Foreign Minister Shahid, and State Councilor Wang Yi, discussed a whole host of issues in the bilateral and multilateral spheres, and agreed to work closely together to address shared interests, in further enhancing the close relations between the two countries.

Minister Shahid thanked the State Councilor and the Chinese Government, for the generous assistance it had provided to the Maldives, including the construction of the China-Maldives Friendship Bridge, the Housing Units in Hulhumale’, and the expansion of the Velana International Airport. Minister Shahid also expressed his gratitude for China’s assistance in providing vaccines and other pandemic related medical supplies to the Maldives, to combat the community spread of the COVID-19 pandemic.

In commemoration of the 50th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries, Foreign Minister Shahid and State Councilor Wang Yi both reiterated that Maldives and China will increase their cooperation both bilaterally, through economic and development cooperation, health cooperation, in international fora such as the United Nations.

State Councilor Wang Yi is presently on an Official Visit to the Maldives, and will also call on His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, President of the Republic of Maldives, during his stay.

en.title: Maldives and China Sign Five Agreements During Official Visit
en.description: China Foreign Minister H.E. Wang Yi and Maldives Foreign Minister Shahid witnessed the signing of a number of key agreements on important areas
en.body:
China Foreign Minister H.E. Wang Yi and Maldives Foreign Minister Shahid witnessed the signing of a number of key agreements on important areas

State Councilor and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People’s Republic of China His Excellency Wang Yi and Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid, today witnessed the signing of a number of key agreements on important areas such as infrastructure development, health, and travel.

The agreements that were signed during the visit were “Agreement on Mutual Visa Exemption between the Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the People’s Republic of China”, which will allow Maldivians to travel to China on a 30-day visa free basis, once the pandemic restrictions have been lifted, and the “Agreement of Economic and Technical Cooperation between the Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the People’s Republic of China on Grand Aid” focusing on development of key areas such as social, livelihood, and infrastructure projects. Both these agreements were signed by His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel on behalf of the Government of Maldives.

His Excellency Mohamed Aslam, the Minister of National Planning, Housing and Infrastructure signed on behalf of the Government, a “Letter of Exchange on the Feasibility Study of Management and Maintenance of China-Maldives Friendship Bridge”. His Excellency Akram Kamauludeen, Minister of State for National Planning, Housing and Infrastructure also signed a “Supplementary Contract to the Implementation Contract for China Aided Micro-Grid Sea-water Desalination Project in the Maldives”.

Finally, His Excellency Ahmed Naseem, Minister of Health, signed the “Agreement on Establishing a Hospital Assistance and Cooperation Programme between the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Maldives and the National Health Commission of the People’s Republic of China.”

The agreements signed today, will directly benefit the people of Maldives, improving their quality of health services, providing additional outlets for sea water desalination, and by assisting the Government with the maintenance of the flagship China-Maldives Friendship Bridge.

en.title: State Councilor Wang Yi Departs Maldives After Official Visit
en.description: State Councilor Wang Yi Departs Maldives After Official Visit
en.body:
State Councilor Wang Yi Departs Maldives After Official Visit

His Excellency Wang Yi, State Councilor and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People’s Republic of China, departed today after concluding his two-day official visit to the Maldives.

During the visit, the State Councilor paid a courtesy call on President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih today. He also led the Chinese Delegation at the bilateral discussions held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

In commemoration of the 50th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries, State Councilor Wang Yi and Foreign Minister Shahid unveiled the official logo symbolising the occasion.

en.title: State Councilor and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People’s Republic of China arrives in Maldives on an official visit
en.description: State Councilor Wang Yi, was received at the Velana International Airport by Foreign Minister Shahid and senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
en.body:
State Councilor Wang Yi, was received at the Velana International Airport by Foreign Minister Shahid and senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The State Councilor and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People’s Republic of China, His Excellency Wang Yi has arrived in the Maldives today on an Official Visit at the invitation of His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives.

State Councilor Wang Yi, was received at the Velana International Airport by Foreign Minister Shahid and senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The visit is a part of both countries efforts to strengthen the long-standing bilateral ties and to commemorate the 50th Anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Maldives and China.

During his visit, State Councilor Wang Yi will pay a courtesy call on His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, President of the Republic of Maldives, and will hold Official Talks with the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid.

State Councilor Wang Yi and Foreign Minister Shahid will also witness the signing of a number of key agreements on important areas such as infrastructure development, health, and travel.

China is one of the most important development partners of the Maldives, and has continued to contribute to the socio-economic development of the country in a number of important areas.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends greetings to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Cuba on the Anniversary of the Cuban Revolution
en.description: Minister Shahid sends greetings to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Cuba on the Anniversary of the Cuban Revolution
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends greetings to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Cuba on the Anniversary of the Cuban Revolution

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends message of felicitations to Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Cuba on the occasion of the Anniversary of the Cuban Revolution.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

It gives me great pleasure to extend sincere felicitations and well wishes to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of Cuba on this auspicious occasion of the 63rd anniversary of the Cuban Revolution.

I remain confident that the bilateral and multilateral cooperation between Maldives and Cuba will continue to strengthen in the years to come.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your good health and well-being, and for further progress of the people of the Republic of Cuba and the assurances of my highest considerations.

en.title: Maldives and the United States of America signs agreement on the G-20 Debt Service Suspension Initiative (DSSI)
en.description: In September, a MOU on the Treatment of Debt Services was signed by Minister Ameer, and the representatives of a number of other creditor countries including US
en.body:
In September, a MOU on the Treatment of Debt Services was signed by Minister Ameer, and the representatives of a number of other creditor countries including US

The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the United States of America signed an agreement on the G-20 Debt Service Suspension Initiative (DSSI), to temporarily suspend debt-service payments owed to bilateral creditors. The agreement was signed on behalf of the Government of the Republic of Maldives by His Excellency Omar Abdul Razzak, High Commissioner of the Republic of Maldives to the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, and on behalf of the Government of the United States of America by Her Excellency Alaina Teplitz, Ambassador of the United States of America to the Republic of Maldives.

The agreement signed today will contribute directly to the Maldives’ ongoing economic recovery efforts, and will improve debt transparency and debt management amidst the present economic challenges. In September this year, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on the Treatment of Debt Services was signed by His Excellency Ibrahim Ameer, Minister of Finance of the Maldives, and the representatives of a number of other creditor countries, including the United States of America.

The Signing Ceremony which was held at the High Commission of the Republic of Maldives in Colombo, Sri Lanka today was attended by senior officials from the High Commission and the Embassy of the United States of America.

en.title: China Foreign Minister to visit Maldives in January 2022
en.description: China Foreign Minister to visit Maldives in January 2022
en.body:
China Foreign Minister to visit Maldives in January 2022

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, will host the State Councilor and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People’s Republic of China, His Excellency Wang Yi, in the Maldives in January 2022.

The State Councilor is visiting the Maldives on an invitation extended by Foreign Minister Shahid during the latter’s visit to China in November 2021.

During his visit to the Maldives, the State Councilor will pay a courtesy call on His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, President of the Republic of Maldives, and will lead the Chinese Delegation during the Official Talks between the two sides. The visit is due to take place on 7 January 2022, and will commemorate the 50th Anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Maldives and China.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Mongolia
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Mongolia
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Mongolia

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of felicitation to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Mongolia, Her Excellency Battsetseg Batmunkh, on the occasion of the Indepdence Day of Mongolia.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

On behalf of the Government and the people of the Republic of Maldives, it gives me great pleasure to extend my sincere greetings to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Mongolia on the joyous occasion of the Independence Day of Mongolia.

I sincerely hope that the bilateral relations between our two countries will further strengthen in the years ahead.

Let me also take this opportunity to extend my best wishes to Your Excellency’s good health and success, and for the continued peace, progress and prosperity of the people of Mongolia.

dv.body:
ތައިލެންޑް ޕާސް ގެ ދަށުން "ޓެސްޓް އެންޑް ގޯ" އަދި "ސޭންޑްބޮކްސް" ސްކީމްތައް މެދުކަނޑާލުން (ޕުކެޓް ސޭންޑްބޮކްސް ނުހިމެނޭ

23 ޑިސެމްބަރު 2021 ކޮވިޑް-19 ގެ އޮމިކްރޮން ވޭރިއަންޓް މުޅި ދުނިޔޭގައި ހަލުވިކަމާއެކު ފެތުރެމުން އަންނާތީ، ތައިލެންޑްގެ ސަރުކާރުން އަޅަމުންގެންދާ ފިޔަވަޅުތައް އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމުގެ ގޮތުން، 22 ޑިސެމްބަރު 2021 ވަނަ ދުވަހުން ފެށިގެން، އަންނަނިވި ފިޔަވަޅުތައް އެޅުމަށް ތައިލެންޑުގެ ކަމާބެހޭ ފަރާތްތަކުން ވަނީ ނިންމާފައެވެ.

1. "ޓެސް އެންޑް ގޯ" ސްކީމްގެ ދަށުން 10 ޖެނުއަރީ 2022 ގެ ކުރިން ތައިލެންޑަށް ދަތުރުކުރަން ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ ފަރާތްތަކުގެ ތެރެއިން 22 ޑިސެމްބަރ 2021 ގެ ކުރިން ތައިލެންޑް ޕާސް QR ކޯޑް ލިބިފައިވާ ފަރާތްތަކަށް "ޓެސްޓް އެންޑް ގޯ" ސްކީމްގެ ދަށުން ތައިލެންޑަށް ދަތުރުކުރެވޭނެއެވެ.
2. 22 ޑިސެމްބަރ 2021 ގެ ކުރިން ތައިލެންޑް ޕާސްއަށް އެޕްލިކޭޝަން ހުށަހަޅާފައިވާ ފަރާތްތަކަށް ވެސް ތައިލެންޑް ޕާސް އެޕްރޫވަލް QR ކޯޑް ލިބުމުން "ޓެސްޓް އެންޑް ގޯ" ސްކީމް ގެ ދަށުން ތައިލެންޑަށް ދަތުރުކުރެވޭނެއެވެ.
3. 22 ޑިސެމްބަރ 2021 އިން ފެށިގެން ތައިލެންޑް ޕާސް އަށް އަލަށް އެޕްލިކޭޝަން ހުށަހަޅުއްވާ ފަރާތްތަކަށް ތައިލެންޑަށް ދަތުރުކުރެވޭނީ އަލްޓަނޭޓިވް ކަރަންޓީނު ނުވަތަ ޕުކެޓް ސޭންޑް ބޮކްސް ސްކީމްގެ ދަށުންނެވެ.
4. "ޓެސްޓް އެންޑް ގޯ" ސްކީމްގެ ދަށުން ތައިލެންޑަށް އެތެރެވެފައިވާ ހުރިހާ ފަރާތްތަކުންވެސް އޮން އަރައިވަލް ޕީސީއާރު ކޮވިޑް ޓެސްޓްގެ އިތުރުން ތައިލެންޑް ސަރުކާރުން ކަނޑައަޅާފައިވާ ފެސިލިޓީއަކުން ދެވަނަ ޕީސީއާރު ކޮވިޑް ޓެސްޓެއް ހަދަންޖެހޭނެއެވެ. މިޓެސްޓަކީ ތައި ސަރުކާރުގެ ޚަރަދުގައި ހިލޭ ހަދާދެވޭ ޓެސްޓެކެވެ.

ވީމާ، ތައިލެންޑަށް ދަތުރުކުރުމަށް މިވަގުތު އައިސްފައިވާ ބަދަލާގުޅިގެން، ތައިލެންޑްގައި ދިރިއުޅޭ އަދި ތައިލެންޑަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ދިވެހިން މިކަމަށް ސަމާލުވުމަށް އެދެމެވެ. އަދި މި ފިޔަވަޅުތަކަށް ބަދަލުއައުން އެކަށީގެންވުމާއެކު، ދަތުރުކުރުމުގެ ކުރިން މައުލޫމާތު ސާފުކުރުމަށްވެސް އެދެމެވެ. މީގެ އިތުރުން، މި ދަނޑިވަޅުގައި ކޮންމެހެން ކުރަންޖެހޭ ދަތުރުތައް ފިޔަވައި، އެހެން ދަތުރުތައް ނުކުރުމަށް އިލްތިމާސްކުރަމެވެ. އަދި ތައިލެންޑްގައި ދިރިއުޅޭ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނާއި އެކިބޭނުންތަކަށް ތައިލެންޑަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުން އެޤައުމުގެ ސަރުކާރުގެ ނިންމުންތަކާއި އެންގުންތަކަށް ސަމާލުވުމަށްވެސް އިލްތިމާސްކުރަމެވެ.

ރާއްޖޭން ބޭރަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނާއި ރާއްޖޭން ބޭރުގައި ދިރިއުޅޭ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުން، މި މިނިސްޓްރީގައާއި އެންމެ ކައިރީގައި ހުންނަ ރާއްޖޭގެ ޑިޕްލޮމެޓިކް މިޝަންގައި ރެޖިސްޓަރ ކުރުމަށްވެސް އިލްތިމާސްކުރަމެވެ. އެގޮތުން، ތައިލެންޑަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނާއި ތައިލެންޑްގައި ދިރިއުޅޭ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުން އެޤައުމުގައި ހުންނަ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އެމްބަސީގައި ރެޖިސްޓަރ ކުރުމަށް އެދެމެވެ.

ހަމައެހެންމެ، ރާއްޖޭން ބޭރަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ދިވެހިން ކޮވިޑް-19 ކަވަރުކުރާ ޓްރެވަލް އިންޝުއަރެންސް ހޯދުމަކީވެސް، ޚާއްޞަކޮށް މި ދުވަސްވަރު ވަރަށް ބޭނުންތެރި ކަމެއްކަމުގައި މި މިނިސްޓްރީއިން ފާހަގަކުރަމެވެ

dv.title: ސިންގަޕޫރަށް ދަތުރުކުރެވޭ ގޮތަށް ހަމަޖައްސާފައިވާ "ވެކްސިނޭޓެޑް ޓްރެވަލް ލޭން (ވީ.ޓީ.އެލް)" ގެ އިންތިޒާމުގެ ދަށުން ޓިކެޓް ވިއްކުން ވަގުތީ ގޮތުން މެދުކަނޑާލުމަށް އެ ޤައުމުން ނިންމުމާ ގުޅޭ
dv.description: ސިންގަޕޫރަށް ދަތުރުކުރެވޭ ގޮތަށް ހަމަޖައްސާފައިވާ "ވެކްސިނޭޓެޑް ޓްރެވަލް ލޭން (ވީ.ޓީ.އެލް)" ގެ އިންތިޒާމުގެ ދަށުން ޓިކެޓް ވިއްކުން ވަގުތީ ގޮތުން މެދުކަނޑާލުމަށް އެ ޤައުމުން ނިންމުމާ ގުޅޭ
dv.body:
ސިންގަޕޫރަށް ދަތުރުކުރެވޭ ގޮތަށް ހަމަޖައްސާފައިވާ "ވެކްސިނޭޓެޑް ޓްރެވަލް ލޭން (ވީ.ޓީ.އެލް)" ގެ އިންތިޒާމުގެ ދަށުން ޓިކެޓް ވިއްކުން ވަގުތީ ގޮތުން މެދުކަނޑާލުމަށް އެ ޤައުމުން ނިންމުމާ ގުޅޭ

ކޮވިޑް19 ވެކްސިން ފުރިހަމަކޮށްފައިވާ ފަރާތްތަކަށް ސިންގަޕޫރަށް ދަތުރުކުރެވޭ ގޮތަށް ހަމަޖައްސާފައިވާ "ވެކްސިނޭޓެޑް ޓްރެވަލް ލޭން (ވީ.ޓީ.އެލް)" ގެ އިންތިޒާމުގެ ދަށުން ޓިކެޓް ވިއްކުން، ދުނިޔޭގައި މިވަގުތު ހަލުވިކަމާއެކު ފެތުރެމުންދާ ކޮވިޑް19 "އޮމިކްރޮން" ވޭރިއެންޓާއި ގުޅިގެން، ވަގުތީ ގޮތުން މެދުކަނޑާލުމަށް އެ ޤައުމުން ނިންމުމާ ގުޅޭ

ދުނިޔޭގައި މި ވަގުތު ހަލުވިކަމާއެކު ފެތުރެމުންދާ ކޮވިޑް19 "އޮމިކްރޮން" ވޭރިއެންޓާ ގުޅިގެން ސިންގަޕޫރުގެ ސަރުކާރުން އަންނަނިވި ފިޔަވަޅުތައް އެޅުމަށް ނިންމާފައިވާކަން މި މިނިސްޓްރީއަށް އަންގަވާފައިވެއެވެ.

1. 22 ޑިސެމްބަރު 2021 ވާ ބުދަ ދުވަހުގެ 23:59 ން ފެށިގެން 20 ޖެނުއަރީ 2020 ގެ 23:59 (ސިންގަޕޫރު ގަޑިން) ގެ ނިޔަލަށް އެ މުއްދަތުގައި ދަތުރުކުރާގޮތަށް ވީ.ޓީ.އެލް އަށް ޚާއްޞަކުރެވިފައިވާ ފްލައިޓުތަކުން ޓިކެޓް ވިއްކުން ހުއްޓާލުން. މި މުއްދަތުގައިވެސް، 21 ޖެނުއަރީ 2022 ގެ ފަހުން ދަތުރުކުރާ ގޮތަށް މި ފްލައިޓުތަކުން ޓިކެޓް ވިއްކުމަށާއި، ނަމަވެސް ވިއްކާ ޓިކެޓުގެ އަދަދު %50 އިންސައްތަ މަދުކުރުން.
2. 22 ޑިސެމްބަރ 2021 ވާ ބުދަ ދުވަހުގެ ސިންގަޕޫރު ގަޑިން 23:59 ގެ ކުރިން ވީ.ޓީ.އެލް ފްލައިޓުތަކުން ޓިކެޓް ނަންގަވާފައިވާ، ވީ.ޓީ.އެލް ގެ ޝަރުޠުތައް ފުރިހަމަ ވާ ފަރާތްތަކަށް ކަރަންޓީނުވުމާ ނުލައި ދަތުރު ކުރެވުން.

މަތީގައިވާ ފިޔަވަޅު ތަކަކީ ވީޓީއެލް އިންތިޒާމު ހުއްޓާލުން ނޫންކަމާއި، "އޮމިކްރޮން" ވޭރިއެންޓާ ގުޅިގެން މި ފިޔަވަޅުތައް މުރާޖައާކުރައްވަމުން ގެންދަވާނެކަން ސިންގަޕޫރުގެ ސަރުކާރުން އަންގަވާފައިވެއެވެ.

ވީމާ ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ސިންގަޕޫރަށް ދަތުރުކުރައްވަން ޓިކެޓް ނަންގަވާ ފައިވާ ފަރާތްތަކާއި އެ ޤައުމަށް ދަތުރުކުރައްވަން ޤަޞްދުކުރާ ފަރާތްތަކުގެ މަޢުލޫމާތަށްޓަކައި މިވާހަކަ ދަންނަވައި މި ފިޔަވަޅުތަކަށް ސަމާލުކަން ދެއްވުމަށް މި މިނިސްޓްރީން އިލްތިމާސް ކުރަމެވެ.

dv.title: ތޫފާން ރާއިގެ ސަބަބުން ފިލިޕީންސްގެ ސޭބޫގައި ހާލުގައިޖެހިފައިތިބި ދިވެހި ދަރިވަރުންނަށް މާލީ އެހީތެރިކަން ދިނުމަށް ސަރުކާރުން ނިންމުމާގުޅޭ

dv.body:
ތޫފާން ރާއިގެ ސަބަބުން ފިލިޕީންސްގެ ސޭބޫގައި ހާލުގައިޖެހިފައިތިބި ދިވެހި ދަރިވަރުންނަށް މާލީ އެހީތެރިކަން ދިނުމަށް ސަރުކާރުން ނިންމުމާގުޅޭ

ފިލިޕީންސްގެ ބައެއް ސަރަޙައްދުތަކަށް އެރި ބާރުގަދަ ތޫފާން "ރައި" ގެ ސަބަބުން އެ ޤައުމުގެ ސޭބޫ ސިޓީގައި ތަޢުލީމު ޙާޞިލުކުރަމުންދާ ދިވެހި ދަރިވަރުންތަކެއް ދިރިއުޅެމުން ދިޔަ ޑޯމިޓަރީއަށް ބޮޑެތި ގެއްލުންތަކެއްވެ، ފެނާއި ކަރަންޓު ކެނޑި، މުއާޞަލާތީ އަދި އެހެނިހެން އަސާސީ ޚިދުމަތްތަކަށް ބުރޫއެރުމުގެ ސަބަބުން ހާލުގައި ޖެހިފައިވާ ދަރިވަރުން، އަސާސީ ޚިދުމަތްތައް ލިބެންހުރި ހިޔާވައްސަކަށް ވަގުތީގޮތުން ބަދަލުވުމަށްޓަކައި، އެންސްޕާއާއި ޒަކާތު ފަންޑު މެދުވެރިކޮށް ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން މާލީ އެހީތެރިކަން ފޯރުކޮށްދިނުމަށް ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އިބްރާހީމް މުޙައްމަދު ޞާލިޙު ނިންމަވައިފިއެވެ. ދަރިވަރުން ދިރިއުޅެމުން ދިޔަ ސަރަޙައްދަށް ކަރަންޓުގެ ޚިދުމަތް ޢިއާދަކޮށް ފެނާއި އެހެނިހެން އަސާސީ ޚިދުމަތްތައް ދިނުމަށް ފިލިޕީންސްގެ ސަރުކާރުން މަސައްކަތްކުރަމުންދާ ކަމަށާއި އެކަމަށް މަހެއްހާ ދުވަސް ހޭދަވާނެކަމަށް ބެލެވޭކަމުގެ މަޢުލޫމާތު ފިލިޕީންސްގެ އެމްބަސީން ދެއްވާފައިވާތީ، މި އެހީ ދިނުމަށް ސަރުކާރުން ނިންމަވާފައިވަނީ 1 (އެކެއް) މަސްދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަށެވެ.

މިގޮތަށް ނިންމެވުމާ ގުޅިގެން، އެ ދަރިވަރުންނަށް މާލީ އެހީތެރިކަން ފޯރުކޮށްދިނުމުގެ މަސައްކަތް މި މިނިސްޓްރީއިން ކަމާގުޅުން ހުރި އިދާރާތަކާއެކު ކުރަމުންގެންދާ ވާހަކަ، ދަރިވަރުންނާއި ދަރިވަރުންގެ ބެލެނިވެރިންގެ މަޢުލޫމާތަށްޓަކައި ދަންނަވަމެވެ.

en.title: Minister of State Ahmed Khaleel participates in the 17th Extraordinary session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers
en.description: Minister of State Ahmed Khaleel participates in the 17th Extraordinary session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers
en.body:
Minister of State Ahmed Khaleel participates in the 17th Extraordinary session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers

The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel today participated in the 17th Extraordinary session of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers to discuss humanitarian situation in Afghanistan. The meeting was convened at the request of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and hosted by the Government of Pakistan, in its capital Islamabad.

In his remarks, State Minister Khaleel expressed concerns about the rapidly deteriorating situation in Afghanistan and its implications for the people of Afghanistan and to the wider region. He highlighted that the Maldives is particularly concerned about the situation of Afghan women and girls, and stressed on the importance of protecting and promoting women’s rights. He also called on all parties to engage in dialogue in good faith and to actively participate in national reconciliation efforts to restore democracy and to reach a political settlement of differences through an Afghan-led, Afghan-owned peace process. Further, he appealed to the international community to engage in efforts that would bring peace, stability, and prosperity to the people of Afghanistan.

The Organization of Islamic Cooperation, comprising of 57 Member States, is an international organization formed to safeguard and protect the interests of the Muslim world. The Maldives became a member of the OIC on 26 July 1976 has since participated in all regular Summits, Extraordinary summits and the Foreign Ministers Meetings.

State Minister Khaleel stated that the Maldives attaches great importance to its relations with Thailand and appreciates the continued assistance and co-operation received from Thailand towards the socio-economic development of Maldives, especially during the fight against the Covid-19 pandemic.

State Minister Khaleel and Ambassador Poj discussed ways to further strengthen the existing friendly bilateral ties, in the area of education, tourism, sports and economic development cooperation.

State Minister Khaleel thanked the Government of Thailand for the hospitality extended to the Maldivians citizens residing in Thailand.

en.title: UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention briefs the Government and Stakeholders on the findings of their visit
en.description: UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention briefs the Government and Stakeholders on the findings of their visit
en.body:
UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention briefs the Government and Stakeholders on the findings of their visit

Foreign Secretary, His Excellency Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed today chaired the debriefing session held by the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention. The Working Group is currently undertaking a country visit to the Maldives from 29 November to 9 December 2021.

During the session held this morning at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Secretary thanked the Working Group for accepting the Government’s Standing Invitation and visiting the Maldives. The Chair-Rapporteur of the Working Group, Ms. Elina Steinerte expressed gratitude to the Government of Maldives for the invitation to undertake this visit and for the cooperation provided to the team. In today’s debriefing, the Working Group gave a brief overview of the preliminary findings of their visit. The Working Group will present its final report on this visit to the UN Human Rights Council in September 2022.

The briefing session was attended by senior officials from Government ministries and relevant stakeholders.

The Working Group on Arbitrary Detention is a Special Procedures mandate-holder of the UN Human Rights Council, established by the former Commission on Human Rights in 1991 to investigate instances of alleged arbitrary deprivation of liberty. The mandate of the Working Group has been extended by the Commission to cover the issue of administrative custody of asylum-seekers and immigrants.

en.title: Minister of State participates in the 14th Bali Democracy Forum
en.description: Minister of State participates in the 14th Bali Democracy Forum
en.body:
Minister of State participates in the 14th Bali Democracy Forum

His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, today participated virtually in the 14th Bali Democracy Forum. The hybrid meeting was hosted by the Government of Indonesia, under the theme “Democracy for Humanity: Advancing Economic and Social Justice during Pandemic”.

State Minister Khaleel participated in the panel discussion concerning democracy and advancing inclusion. In his remarks, the State Minister highlighted the importance of the Forum for sharing experiences and best practices towards strengthening democratic systems. He also noted that the socio-economic problems that has accumulated over the years have been exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. Furthermore, he emphasized the importance of ensuring women’s inclusion and elaborated on the efforts undertaken by the current administration to ensure justice for women and girls. He also stressed on the importance of vaccine equity and urged countries to work together in multilateral solidarity with renewed motivation to recover from the pandemic.

US Secretary of State Antony Blinken, Minister of Foreign Affairs of New Zealand Nanaia Mahuta, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Turkey Mevlüt Çavuşoğlu and the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Michelle Bachelet also participated in this discussion.

Founded in 2008, the Bali Democracy Forum is an annual international forum held in Bali, Indonesia. The Forum allows Ministers, Senior Government officials, experts and relevant organizations to come together and share valuable best practices and lesson learnt on building democratic societies.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends congratulatory message on the occasion of the 37th SAARC Charter Day
en.description: Minister Shahid sends congratulatory message on the occasion of the 37th SAARC Charter Day
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends congratulatory message on the occasion of the 37th SAARC Charter Day

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sent a congratulatory message to the SAARC Secretariat on the occasion of the 37th SAARC Charter Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It gives me great pleasure to extend warm greetings and best wishes to the Secretary General of SAARC, the SAARC Secretariat and people of the SAARC region, on the happy occasion of SAARC Charter Day.

Today as we celebrate 37th year of the founding of SAARC, it is important to reflect on the successes and gains achieved by SAARC despite the multifarious challenges. South Asia is a region blessed with great potential and all Member States must renew their commitment to work hand in hand, to reap the benefits of regional cooperation to enhance prosperity and quality of life of South Asian people.

Across the globe, and in the South Asia region, we continue to battle the Covid-19 pandemic. We recognize and commend the contributions of SAARC in bringing Member States together, in pursuing our collective efforts to recover from the social and economic impacts of Covid-19. It is my sincere hope that this spirit of solidarity and commitment is, and will continue to manifest in all areas of cooperation.

As we commemorate this special occasion, let me assure the full support of the Government of Maldives to foster regional cooperation, as enshrined in the SAARC Charter.”

During the ceremony, His Majesty the King congratulated Ambassador Khaleel on the commencement of his term and expressed confidence that the appointment of the first Non-Resident Ambassador to Jordan by President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih on the 40th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relationship between the two countries, would further strengthen the alliance between the two countries.

Ambassador Khaleel assured of his commitment to work with the Kingdom of Jordan in strengthening cooperation between the two countries, in areas of mutual interest.

Ambassador Khaleel was accompanied to the ceremony by the Minister-Counsellor of the Embassy of Maldives in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Badoora Saeed. The ceremony was attended by the Chief of the Royal Hashemite Court of Jordan Yousef Issawi, and the Acting Foreign Minister and Minister of Political and Parliamentary Affairs of Jordan, Musa Maaytah.

en.title: Foreign Secretary Ghafoor participates in the 10th Anniversary Ministerial Meeting of the Freedom Online Coalition
en.description: Foreign Secretary Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed participates in the 10th Anniversary Ministerial Meeting of the Freedom Online Coalition
en.body:
Foreign Secretary Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed participates in the 10th Anniversary Ministerial Meeting of the Freedom Online Coalition

Foreign Secretary Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed today participated in the 10th Anniversary Ministerial Meeting of the Freedom Online Coalition (FOC). The virtual meeting was hosted by the Government of Finland, Chair of the FOC, under the theme, “Openness, Accessibility and inclusion – Human Rights Online in the 2020’s”.

In his remarks, the Foreign Secretary congratulated the FOC for a successful 10 year anniversary and noted that the meeting was a testament of the strength of the Coalition. He reaffirmed the commitment of the Government of Maldives to promote and protect human rights and fundamental freedoms. He further elaborated on the efforts undertaken by the current administration to promote freedom of expression and opinion. In this regard, Foreign Secretary Ghafoor highlighted the repealing of the Anti-Defamation Act in 2018, and the reduction in Internet prices across the Maldives. He concluded his remarks by reiterating the commitment of the Maldives to work within the FOC to promote internet freedom and to protect and promote human rights online.

The FOC is a leading group of countries working together to advance internet freedom and promote the human rights and fundamental freedoms enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Since its founding conference in 2011, the FOC has grown from 15 members to 34 today.

en.title: Foreign Secretary meets the Chair-Rapporteur of the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention
en.description: Foreign Secretary meets the Chair-Rapporteur of the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention
en.body:
Foreign Secretary meets the Chair-Rapporteur of the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention

Foreign Secretary, His Excellency Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed today met with the Chair-Rapporteur of the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention, Ms. Elina Steinerte. The Chair-Rapporteur is currently undertaking a country visit to the Maldives from 29 November to 10 December 2021.

During the meeting held this morning, the Foreign Secretary welcomed the Working Group to the Maldives and expressed gratitude for accepting the Government’s Standing Invitation. The Chair-Rapporteur took positive note of the fact that the Maldives has made remarkable progress to promote and protect human rights and briefed the Foreign Secretary concerning issues regarding the Working Group’s mandate on arbitrary detention. The Foreign Secretary reiterated the commitment of the Government to fully cooperate with the Working Group and assured the Chair-Rapporteur that the Maldives will welcome the recommendations of the Working Group and work closely to implement them.

The Working Group will share their preliminary observations at a press conference on 9 December 2021. The Working Group will present its final report on this visit to the UN Human Rights Council in September 2022.

Foreign Secretary was accompanied by Ahmed Shiaan, Additional Secretary, Mariyam Reesha, Director-General at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mohamed Aseel Hassan, Legal Counsel at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Adam Hamid, Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The working group comprised of Ms. Leigh TOOMEY, Member of WGAD, Ms. Priya Gopalan, Member of WGAD Ms. Lucie VIERSMA, Member of WGAD Ms. Margarita NECHAEVA, Human Rights Officer The Working Group on Arbitrary Detention is a Special Procedures mandate-holder of the UN Human Rights Council, established by the former Commission on Human Rights in 1991 to investigate instances of alleged arbitrary deprivation of liberty. The mandate of the Working Group has been extended by the Commission to cover the issue of administrative custody of asylum-seekers and immigrants.

en.title: Foreign Secretary of Bangladesh departs Maldives
en.description: Foreign Secretary of Bangladesh departs Maldives
en.body:
Foreign Secretary of Bangladesh departs Maldives

The Foreign Secretary of Bangladesh Ambassador Masud Bin Momen departed Maldives this afternoon after concluding his official visit to Maldives. Foreign Secretary Momen was on a two-day official visit on the invitation of Foreign Secretary of Maldives, Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, to hold the first Bilateral Consultations between Maldives and Bangladesh.

During the visit, the Foreign Secretaries held official consultations to review ongoing and discuss new areas of bilateral cooperation between both countries.

Foreign Secretary Ambassador Masud Bin Momen also called on Vice President Faisal Naseem, Minister of Economic Development Uz. Fayyaz Ismail and Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel.

This is Foreign Secretary Momen’s first visit to the Maldives, since assuming his office on 31 December 2019. Foreign Secretary Momen and delegation were seen off at Velana International Airport by Foreign Secretary Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, Chief of Protocol Aishath Shaan Shakir and Joint Secretary Fathimath Ghina.

en.title: Foreign Secretaries of Maldives and Bangladesh hold Bilateral Consultations.
en.description: Foreign Secretaries of Maldives and Bangladesh hold Bilateral Consultations.
en.body:
Foreign Secretaries of Maldives and Bangladesh hold Bilateral Consultations.

he Foreign Secretary of Maldives, Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed and the Foreign Secretary of Bangladesh, Masud Bin Momen held the first Bilateral Consultations,. as prescribed under the MoU on the Establishment of Bilateral Consultations signed between the two countries earlier this year.

During the consultations held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today, both Foreign Secretaries reflected on the long history of close relations between Maldives and Bangladesh, which has been elevated to much higher levels in recent months.

The two Foreign Secretaries reviewed the entire spectrum of cooperation and engagements between the two countries, and discussed the strengthening and deepening of the multi-faceted relationship between Maldives and Bangladesh.

In their discussion, particular emphasis was laid on accelerating the implementation of the agreements signed between Maldives and Bangladesh recently, and to expedite the conclusion of other important pending agreements.

Increasing connectivity and bilateral trade between the two nations were highlighted by Foreign Secretary Momen. Foreign Secretary Ghafoor noted the importance of cooperation in higher education and development of human resources, training and capacity building, in particular for the health sector of Maldives. Other areas of discussion included cooperation in climate change, culture, fisheries and agriculture.

Foreign Secretary Ghafoor expressed gratitude to the Government of Bangladesh for the continued support and commitment extended to the Government and the people of the Maldives, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Foreign Secretary Masud Bin Momen, along with a high-level delegation from the Government of Bangladesh is on a two-day official visit to the Maldives.
